chapter: Sue and Patsy Howard in show business
title: Walking out over unpaid wages at the Rum Boogie
summary: Patsy describes demanding pay before the show, AGVA's reluctance, and the cast fleeing out the back.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: And you were saying you didn't get your money when Mr. Cohen had the club.

Well, for awhile, and he owed us something like two or three weeks, and we had to go to the labor board. In fact, even AGVA was afraid of him, because I insisted on not doing the show because he had promised the money that

Saturday night and when we got to work, I asked where Mr. Cohen was and his henchman said he was in the hospital sick, so I said well, we're not doing a show, because he promised to pay us before the first show.

So he tried to get rough with us, so I called AGVA and AGVA came over and said, oh, Pat, go on and do the show, they'll pay you, instead of standing up for us, so I insisted on not doing the show, said I got to talk to Mr. Cohen. He said, he's in the hospital, and I said, well, get him on the phone so he called him and he said well, "Go on and do the show and I'll pay you tonight." So we went on and did the show and that night put the drop light down on the dance floor, and as they paid the waiters, they would beat them up and throw them out.
So we went out the back door, including the chefs and everybody else. We wouldn't even wait to get our money.
